name: telegram-call
author: Keith Yeung
description: Synthesizes spoken audio from text via a local Kokoro-FastAPI server and places a 1-on-1 Telegram voice call that plays it. Self-installs and self-authenticates on first use; auth has a dedicated verification tool so a wrong code can be retried without invalidating it.

tools.name: synthesize_speech
tools.description: Convert a text message into an mp3 audio file using a local Kokoro-FastAPI server (default http://localhost:8880, override via KOKORO_URL env). Returns the absolute path of the generated audio file. Use this whenever the user asks to call someone with a spoken message rather than a pre-recorded file (e.g. 'call @alice about a possible gas leak'): first call this tool with the spoken text, then pass the returned path to `make_call` as `audio_path`. Results are cached by (voice, speed, text) hash so calling twice with the same args is free.

text.description: The message to speak. Should be a complete, natural-sounding spoken message — write it the way you'd say it out loud. Example: 'Hi Alice, this is an automated alert. There may be a gas leak in your house. Please check immediately and call emergency services if you smell gas.'

voice.description: Optional Kokoro voice name (e.g. 'af_heart', 'af_bella', 'af_nova', 'am_michael', 'bf_emma', 'bm_george'). Defaults to 'af_heart' or the KOKORO_VOICE env var.

speed.description: Optional speech rate multiplier (1.0 = normal, 0.5 = slow, 1.5 = fast). Defaults to 1.0.

tools.name: verify_telegram_code
tools.description: Submit a Telegram verification code (or 2FA cloud password) during the one-time login flow. ONLY use this AFTER `make_call` returned a message asking for a code or password — never as the first step. The tool figures out from internal state whether to verify a `code` or a `password`; pass whichever one the user supplied. If Telegram rejects the value as invalid (a typo), the auth state is preserved so you can retry by calling this tool again with a corrected value — do NOT call `make_call` with `phone` again, that would invalidate the code that was already sent. After this tool succeeds you can call `make_call` to place the actual call.

code.description: The verification code Telegram sent to the user (typically 5 digits, no spaces or dashes). Provide this when `make_call` returned a 'verification code was sent' message.

password.description: The user's Telegram 2FA cloud password. Provide this when verification returned a '2FA enabled' message asking for `password`.

tools.name: make_call
tools.description: Place a 1-on-1 Telegram voice call to a user, play an audio file, and hang up. The very first invocation transparently sets up Python dependencies (~30-90s) and walks the user through a one-time Telegram login. The login flow is: (a) call `make_call` with `phone` set to the user's Telegram number to trigger an SMS/in-app verification code; (b) call the SEPARATE `verify_telegram_code` tool with the `code` (and `password` if 2FA is enabled) — DO NOT call `make_call` with `phone` again after a code has been sent or you will invalidate it; (c) once verification succeeds, call `make_call` again with `target` and `audio_path` to actually place the call. If the user asked you to convey a spoken message (no pre-recorded file given), first call `synthesize_speech` to turn the text into an mp3, then pass that path here as `audio_path`. If `target` is missing, ASK the user — do not invent one.

target.description: Who to call on Telegram. Accepts @username, numeric user_id, or +phone_number (phone numbers only resolve if that user is already in the caller's Telegram contacts; prefer @username when in doubt). If the user has not specified a target, ASK them rather than guessing.

audio_path.description: Absolute path to the audio file to play during the call. Any format ffmpeg can decode is accepted (mp3, wav, ogg, m4a, opus, ...). Typically obtained by first calling `synthesize_speech` with the spoken text.

message.description: Human-readable description of the call, surfaced in the success/failure output.

phone.description: ONE-TIME Telegram account phone number with international country code, e.g. +447700900000. Only provide this on the FIRST authentication step to trigger a verification code. Do NOT include `phone` again after a code has been sent (use `verify_telegram_code` instead) and do NOT include it on normal calls once authenticated.
